extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (registered patent attorneys and patent agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO rules describing ethical and professional obligations for persons practicing before the Office, covering competence, client relations, conflicts, confidentiality, trust accounting, advertising, firm responsibilities, and disciplinary matters. Intended to govern conduct of patent practitioners, firms, and related personnel when representing clients or interacting with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.101 Competence
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall provide competent representation to a client. Competent representation requires the legal, scientific, and technical knowledge, skill, thoroughness and preparation reasonably necessary for the representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.102 Scope of representation and allocation of authority between client and practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of representation and, as required by § 11.104, shall consult with the client as to the means by which they are to be pursued. A practitioner may limit the scope of representation if reasonable with informed consent and shall not counsel or assist a client in conduct the practitioner knows is criminal or fraudulent, though may discuss legal consequences and assist in good-faith legal analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner may take impliedly authorized actions to carry out representation; must consult on means when required by § 11.104; limitation of scope requires informed consent; may discuss legal consequences even if not assisting criminal/fraudulent conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.103 Diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.104 Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly inform client of decisions or circumstances requiring informed consent, reasonably consult about means to accomplish objectives, keep client reasonably informed about status, promptly comply with reasonable information requests, and consult about limitations on the practitioner's conduct when client expects assistance not permitted by the Rules or law. Practitioner shall explain matters to extent reasonably necessary for client's informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.105 Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not make an agreement for, charge, or collect an unreasonable fee or an unreasonable amount for expenses. The scope and basis or rate of the fee and expenses shall be communicated to the client, preferably in writing, before or within a reasonable time after commencing representation. Contingent fees allowed except where prohibited by law and must be in writing with specified terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for reasonableness include: (1) time and labor required, novelty/difficulty, skill required; (2) likelihood employment will preclude other employment; (3) customary local fees; (4) amount involved and results obtained; (5) time limitations; (6) nature/length of professional relationship; (7) experience/reputation/ability of practitioner(s); (8) whether fee is fixed or contingent. Contingent fee agreements must state method of calculation, expenses, whether expenses deducted before/after contingent fee, notify client of expenses liability, and provide written statement upon conclusion showing remittance if recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.106 Confidentiality of information
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not reveal information relating to representation unless client gives informed consent, disclosure is impliedly authorized to carry out the representation, disclosure is permitted by specific exceptions, or disclosure is required by other provisions. Practitioner may reveal information to prevent death/substantial bodily harm, prevent client from engaging in inequitable conduct before the Office or crime/fraud reasonably certain to result in substantial injury to another when client used practitioner's services, to secure legal advice about compliance, to establish claim/defense on behalf of practitioner, or to comply with other law/court order. A practitioner shall disclose to the Office information necessary to comply with duty of disclosure provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists six exceptions where disclosure may be reasonable; also notes implied authorization to reveal information to the extent necessary to carry out representation; ties to duty of disclosure to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.107 Conflict of interest; Current clients
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent a client if the representation involves a concurrent conflict of interest (directly adverse representation of one client to another, or significant risk representation materially limited by responsibilities to another client/former client/third person/personal interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: practitioner may represent despite concurrent conflict if (1) reasonably believes can provide competent and diligent representation to each affected client; (2) representation not prohibited by law; (3) representation does not involve one client asserting a claim against another client represented by the practitioner in the same litigation or proceeding; (4) each affected client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.108 Conflict of interest; Current clients; Specific rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific prohibitions and rules regarding business transactions with clients, using information to client's disadvantage, solicitation of substantial gifts, literary/media rights, financial assistance to clients, accepting compensation from third parties, aggregate settlements, agreements limiting liability, acquisition of proprietary interests in client's cause or proceeding, and firm-wide application of prohibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules include: business transactions with a client allowed only if transaction is fair/reasonable and fully disclosed in writing and client is advised to seek independent counsel and client gives informed consent in writing; cannot use information to client's disadvantage absent informed consent; cannot solicit substantial gifts; cannot negotiate literary/media rights prior to conclusion of representation; limited exceptions for advancing costs/expenses; cannot accept compensation from third party unless client consents, independence preserved, and information protected; aggregate settlements require written informed consent with disclosure; cannot prospectively limit malpractice liability unless client independently represented; limited exceptions allowing liens, contingent fees, and taking interest in patent/application as part of fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.109 Duties to former clients
rubrics_metrics.description: A former practitioner shall not represent another person in the same or substantially related matter materially adverse to the former client's interests unless former client gives informed consent in writing. Practitioner shall not knowingly represent a person in same or substantially related matter in which former firm had represented a client whose interests are materially adverse and about whom the practitioner had acquired protected material information, unless former client gives written informed consent. Practitioner shall not use or reveal information relating to former representation to the disadvantage of the former client except as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.110 Imputation of conflicts of interest; General rule
rubrics_metrics.description: While practitioners are associated in a firm, none shall knowingly represent a client when any one of them practicing alone would be prohibited by §§ 11.107 or 11.109, unless the prohibition is based on a personal interest that does not present significant risk of materially limiting representation or arises out of association with a prior firm where timely screening and written notice to affected former client occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the conditions for effective screening when prohibition arises from disqualified practitioner's association with a prior firm, including apportionment of no part of fee and notice describing screening procedures; addresses firm's ability to represent after practitioner's termination; disqualification may be waived by affected client under § 11.107.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.111 Former or current Federal Government employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who is a former or current Federal Government employee shall not engage in any conduct contrary to applicable Federal ethics law, including conflict of interest statutes and regulations of the department, agency or commission formerly or currently employing the practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.112 Former judge, arbitrator, mediator or other third-party neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent anyone in connection with a matter in which the practitioner participated personally and substantially as a judge or other adjudicative officer or law clerk or as an arbitrator/mediator/third-party neutral unless all parties give informed consent in writing. Practitioner shall not negotiate for employment with any person involved as a party or practitioner in a matter in which the practitioner is participating personally and substantially as a judge/neutral. If disqualified, practitioners associated in a firm must be screened and notice given to parties/tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include arbitrator selected as a partisan of a party in a multimember arbitration panel who may subsequently represent that party.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.113 Organization as client
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner employed or retained by an organization represents the organization acting through its duly authorized constituents. If practitioner knows an organizational constituent is engaged in or intends action that is a violation of law or legal obligation likely to result in substantial injury to the organization, the practitioner shall proceed as reasonably necessary in the organization's best interest (refer the matter to higher authority), and if highest authority fails to address it, may reveal information to prevent substantial injury to the organization to the extent reasonably necessary. Practitioner must explain identity of client when organization's interests are adverse to constituents and may represent both organization and constituent subject to § 11.107.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes steps to take when reporting up within organization and limited circumstances for disclosure outside organization; if dual representation requires consent by appropriate official other than the individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.114 Client with diminished capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: When a client's capacity is diminished, the practitioner shall as far as reasonably possible maintain a normal client-practitioner relationship. If practitioner reasonably believes client is at risk of substantial harm and cannot act in client's interest, practitioner may take reasonably necessary protective action (consult others, seek guardian ad litem/conservator). Information relating to such a client is protected but practitioner is impliedly authorized to reveal information reasonably necessary to protect client's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.115 Safekeeping property
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall hold property of clients or third persons separate from practitioner's own property. Funds must be kept in separate accounts in proper jurisdictions; other property must be identified and safeguarded. Complete records preserved for five years after termination. Advance fees must be deposited into client trust account and withdrawn only as earned or expenses incurred. Promptly notify clients upon receipt of funds/property, deliver funds/property client is entitled to, and render accounting upon request. When multiple claimants claim interests, property must be kept separate until dispute resolved and undisputed portions promptly distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive recordkeeping requirements: receipt/disbursement journals; ledger records per client; copies of retainer/compensation agreements; accountings; bills; records showing disbursements; equivalents of checkbook registers, bank statements, canceled checks; records of electronic transfers with authorizing person and confirmations; monthly trial balances and quarterly reconciliations; copies of client file portions related to trust transactions. Client trust account safeguards: authorized signatories limited to practitioner or persons under direct supervision; receipts deposited intact; withdrawals by check payable to named payee or authorized electronic transfer only. Records may be maintained electronically if printable. Lawyers' records meeting state requirements deemed compliant; rules for firms employing patent agents also stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.116 Declining or terminating representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent or must withdraw if representation will result in violation of the Rules or other law, practitioner's physical/mental condition materially impairs ability, or practitioner is discharged. Practitioner may withdraw where withdrawal can be accomplished without material adverse effect, client persists in criminal/fraudulent course, client used practitioner's services to perpetrate crime/fraud, client insists on repugnant action, client fails substantially to fulfill obligations after reasonable warning, representation imposes unreasonable financial burden or is rendered unreasonably difficult, or other good cause. Practitioner must comply with law or tribunal orders regarding notice/permission to withdraw and must take reasonable steps to protect client's interests on termination (notice, allow time for new counsel, surrender papers, refund unearned advance fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.117 Sale of law practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner or law firm may sell or purchase a law practice or area of practice if seller ceases to engage in private practice in that geographic area, entire practice/area of practice is sold to lawyers or law firms (with exception permitting sale of patent practice only to registered practitioners or firms including a registered practitioner), seller gives written notice to each client regarding proposed sale, client's right to retain other counsel or take file, and client's consent to transfer presumed if client does not object within 90 days; fees shall not be increased because of sale. If client cannot be given notice, transfer requires court order and limited in camera disclosure permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.118 Duties to prospective client
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who discusses possibility of forming client-practitioner relationship is a prospective client. Even when no relationship ensues, practitioner shall not use or reveal information learned in consultation except as § 11.109 would permit for former client. Practitioner subject to these restrictions shall not represent a client with materially adverse interests in same or substantially related matter if practitioner received information from prospective client that could be significantly harmful to that person, except as allowed by written informed consent or where reasonable measures were taken to avoid exposure to more disqualifying information than necessary with screening and notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.201 Advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: In representing a client, a practitioner shall exercise independent professional judgment and render candid advice. Practitioner may refer to law and other considerations such as moral, economic, social and political factors relevant to client's situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.203 Evaluation for use by third persons
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may provide an evaluation of a matter affecting a client for use by someone other than the client if practitioner reasonably believes evaluation is compatible with other aspects of relationship. If evaluation is likely to affect client's interests materially and adversely, practitioner shall not provide it unless client gives informed consent. Except as disclosure authorized in connection with a report of an evaluation, information relating to the evaluation is otherwise protected by § 11.106.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.204 Practitioner serving as third-party neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner serves as a third-party neutral when assisting two or more persons who are not clients to reach a resolution (e.g., arbitrator, mediator). Practitioner serving as neutral shall inform unrepresented parties that practitioner is not representing them and shall explain difference between neutral role and representative role when a party does not understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.301 Meritorious claims and contentions
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not bring or defend a proceeding, or assert or controvert an issue therein, unless there is a basis in law and fact for doing so that is not frivolous, which includes a good-faith argument for an extension, modification or reversal of existing law.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.302 Expediting proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall make reasonable efforts to expedite proceedings before a tribunal consistent with the interests of the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.303 Candor toward the tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not knowingly make a false statement of fact or law to a tribunal or fail to correct a false statement of material fact or law previously made; fail to disclose controlling adverse legal authority in inter partes or ex parte proceedings when known; or offer evidence the practitioner knows to be false. If material evidence is later known to be false, practitioner shall take reasonable remedial measures, including disclosure if necessary. Practitioner who knows a person intends or has engaged in criminal or fraudulent conduct related to proceeding shall take reasonable remedial measures, including disclosure when necessary. These duties continue to the conclusion of the proceeding and may require disclosure of otherwise protected information. In ex parte proceedings, practitioner shall inform tribunal of all material facts known enabling informed decision. In proceedings before the Office, practitioner shall disclose information necessary to comply with duty of disclosure provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.304 Fairness to opposing party and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not unlawfully obstruct access to evidence or alter/destroy/conceal material having potential evidentiary value, falsify evidence or counsel a witness to testify falsely, offer inducements to witnesses prohibited by law, knowingly disobey tribunal rules except open refusal asserting no valid obligation, make frivolous discovery requests or fail to make diligent effort to comply with proper discovery, allude at proceedings to matters not reasonably believed relevant or unsupported by admissible evidence, assert personal knowledge of facts in issue except when testifying, state personal opinions as to justness/credibility/culpability/guilt, or request a non-client to refrain from voluntarily giving relevant information except limited circumstances for relatives/employees/agents with no adverse effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.305 Impartiality and decorum of the tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not seek to influence judges, hearing officers, administrative judges, jurors, Office employees or other officials by means prohibited by law; shall not communicate ex parte with such persons during the proceeding unless authorized by law, rule or court order; and shall not engage in conduct intended to disrupt proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.306 Trial publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner participating in investigation or litigation shall not make extrajudicial statements that the practitioner knows or reasonably should know will be disseminated by public communication and will have a substantial likelihood of materially prejudicing an adjudicative proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.403 Dealing with unrepresented person
rubrics_metrics.description: In dealing on behalf of a client with an unrepresented person, a practitioner shall not state or imply the practitioner is disinterested. When practitioner knows or reasonably should know the unrepresented person misunderstands the practitioner's role, practitioner shall correct misunderstanding. Practitioner shall not give legal advice to an unrepresented person other than advice to secure counsel if practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the unrepresented person's interests are or may be in conflict with client's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.404 Respect for rights of third persons
rubrics_metrics.description: In representing a client, a practitioner shall not use means that have no substantial purpose other than to embarrass, delay, or burden a third person, or use methods of obtaining evidence that violate the legal rights of such a person. A practitioner who receives a document or ESI that was inadvertently sent and knows or reasonably should know it was inadvertently sent shall promptly notify the sender.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.501 Responsibilities of partners, managers, and supervisory practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A partner or practitioner with comparable managerial authority shall make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures giving reasonable assurance that all practitioners conform to the Rules. A supervisory practitioner shall make reasonable efforts to ensure those supervised conform. A practitioner shall be responsible for another practitioner's violation if practitioner orders or ratifies the conduct or is partner/manager/supervisor who knows of the conduct when consequences can be avoided or mitigated but fails to take reasonable remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.502 Responsibilities of a subordinate practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner is bound by the Rules notwithstanding that the practitioner acted at the direction of another. A subordinate practitioner does not violate the Rules if acting in accordance with a supervisory practitioner's reasonable resolution of an arguable question of professional duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.503 Responsibilities regarding non-practitioner assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a non-practitioner assistant employed/retained/associated with a practitioner: partners/managers must make reasonable efforts to ensure the person's conduct is compatible with practitioner's professional obligations; supervisory practitioners must make reasonable efforts to ensure compatibility; and a practitioner shall be responsible for such a person's conduct that would be a violation if engaged in by a practitioner when the practitioner orders or ratifies the conduct or is partner/manager/supervisor and knows of the conduct when consequences can be avoided or mitigated but fails to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.504 Professional independence of a practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner or law firm shall not share legal fees with a non-practitioner except limited exceptions (payments after death, purchase price to estate, inclusion of non-practitioner employees in compensation plans, sharing fees with qualifying nonprofit). Practitioner shall not form a partnership with a non-practitioner if any partnership activities consist of practice of law; shall not permit a person who recommends/employs/pays practitioner to direct/regulate practitioner's professional judgment; shall not practice with a profitable professional corporation where non-practitioner owns interest or directs professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.505 Unauthorized practice of law
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not practice law in a jurisdiction in violation of that jurisdiction's regulation of the legal profession, or assist another in doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.506 Restrictions on right to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not participate in offering or making agreements (partnership, shareholders, employment, etc.) that restrict the practitioner's right to practice after termination of relationship, except agreements concerning retirement benefits; nor participate in agreements where restriction on right to practice is part of settlement of a client controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.507 Responsibilities regarding law-related services
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall be subject to the Rules with respect to provision of law-related services if such services are provided by the practitioner in circumstances not distinct from legal services to clients, or by an entity controlled by the practitioner if practitioner fails to take reasonable measures to assure person obtaining law-related services knows those services are not legal services and that client-practitioner protections do not exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.701 Communications concerning a practitioner's services
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not make a false or misleading communication about the practitioner or the practitioner's services. A communication is false or misleading if it contains a material misrepresentation of fact or law, or omits a fact necessary to make the statement as a whole not materially misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.702 Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §§ 11.701 and 11.703, a practitioner may advertise services through written, recorded or electronic communication, including public media. A practitioner shall not give anything of value for recommending practitioner's services except limited exceptions (pay reasonable ad costs, pay for law practice in accordance with § 11.117, refer clients under nonexclusive reciprocal referral agreement with disclosure). Communications must include the name and office address of at least one practitioner or law firm responsible for its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal referral agreements allowed if nonexclusive and client informed of existence and nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.703 Direct contact with prospective clients
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not by in-person, live telephone or real-time electronic contact solicit professional employment from a prospective client when a significant motive is practitioner's pecuniary gain, unless the person contacted is a practitioner or has a family/close personal/prior professional relationship. Practitioner shall not solicit professional employment from a prospective client by written/recorded/electronic communication or by in-person/telephone/real-time contact if the prospective client has made known they do not want to be solicited or the solicitation involves coercion, duress or harassment. Soliciting communications to known-need prospective clients must include 'Advertising Material' labeling. Exceptions permit participation in prepaid/group legal service plans operated by organizations not owned/directed by practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.704 Communication of fields of practice and specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may communicate the fact that the practitioner does or does not practice in particular fields of law. Registered practitioners who are attorneys may use designations like 'Patents', 'Patent Attorney', etc., and registered practitioners who are not attorneys may use 'Patents', 'Patent Agent', 'Registered Patent Agent' designations. A practitioner shall not state or imply certification as a specialist unless certified by an approved/accredited organization and the certifying organization's name is clearly identified. Persons granted limited recognition may use 'Limited Recognition.'

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.705 Firm names and letterheads
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not use a firm name, letterhead or other professional designation that violates § 11.701. Trade names may be used if they do not imply connection with government or public/charitable legal services organization and do not otherwise violate § 11.701. The name of a practitioner holding public office shall not be used in the name of a firm or communications on its behalf during any substantial period when the practitioner is not actively and regularly practicing with the firm.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.801 Registration, recognition and disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for registration or recognition to practice before the Office, or a practitioner in connection with an application for registration/recognition or disciplinary/reinstatement matter, shall not knowingly make a false statement of material fact or fail to disclose a fact necessary to correct a misapprehension known to have arisen, fail to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation, or knowingly fail to respond to a lawful demand or request for information from an admissions or disciplinary authority, except where disclosure is protected by § 11.106.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.802 Judicial and legal officials
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not make a statement the practitioner knows to be false or with reckless disregard as to its truth concerning the qualifications or integrity of a judge, adjudicatory officer or public legal officer, or a candidate for such office. A practitioner who is a candidate for judicial office shall comply with applicable Code of Judicial Conduct provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.803 Reporting professional misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who knows another practitioner has committed a violation of the Rules raising a substantial question as to honesty, trustworthiness or fitness shall inform the OED Director and any other appropriate professional authority. A practitioner who knows a judicial official has committed a violation raising a substantial question as to fitness shall inform appropriate authority. This section does not require disclosure of information protected by § 11.106 or information gained while participating in an approved lawyers assistance program.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.804 Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct for a practitioner to violate or attempt to violate the Rules, knowingly assist or induce another to do so, commit a criminal act reflecting adversely on honesty/trustworthiness/fitness, engage in dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation, engage in conduct prejudicial to administration of justice, state or imply an ability to improperly influence a government agency/official or achieve results by unlawful means, knowingly assist a judicial officer or Office employee in conduct violating rules or law, be publicly disciplined on ethical/professional misconduct grounds by a state, the United States, or the country in which the practitioner resides, or engage in other conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.901 Savings clause
rubrics_metrics.description: A disciplinary proceeding based on conduct engaged in prior to the effective date of these regulations may be instituted subsequent to such effective date if such conduct would continue to justify disciplinary sanctions under this part. No practitioner shall be subject to a disciplinary proceeding under this part based on conduct engaged in before the effective date if such conduct would not have been subject to disciplinary action before such effective date.
